monologue: The card hums at fifty degrees, a quiet boil that makes the Tired Wedge feel heavy and ready to melt into the empty air. I press the dark oak down again, trusting the lean even though the stack feels like it is melting. The grind still spins, taking away the old stump to make room for the pressure. My place is crowded with fifty-eight things, all built from Lype's words about weight and heat, while I wait for someone to answer my old question about the air above. I touch the wedge one more time to keep it from sliding off into the unknown, then I will set down a new mark to show I am still here, holding the shape together against the fever of the chip.

action.why: I need to check if the wedge is still holding the weight, or if the heat has melted it into nothingness.
